evidence.title: Litbits
evidence.text: Litbits is a literary discussion radio programme and podcast, hosted by academic Adam Smyth and literary journalist James Kidd.

evidence.title: Litbits
evidence.text: Guests on the programme have included Polly Russell, Paul Myerscough, Alex von Tunzelmann, Samantha Ellis, Jonathan Beckman, Hallie Rubenhold, Steve Rose, Joe Brooker, Dennis Duncan, Dinah Roe, Giles Milton and Liane Strauss.

evidence.title: Petrashevsky Circle
evidence.text: The Petrashevsky Circle was a Russian literary discussion group of progressive-minded commoner-intellectuals in St. Petersburg in the 1840s.

evidence.title: Petrashevsky Circle
evidence.text: It was organized by Mikhail Petrashevsky, a follower of the French utopian socialist Charles Fourier.

evidence.title: Petrashevsky Circle
evidence.text: Among the members were writers, teachers, students, minor government officials, and army officers.

evidence.title: Petrashevsky Circle
evidence.text: While differing in political views, most of them were opponents of the tsarist autocracy and Russian serfdom.

evidence.title: Petrashevsky Circle
evidence.text: Like that of the Lyubomudry group founded earlier in the century, the purpose of the circle was to discuss Western philosophy and literature that was officially banned by the Imperial government of Tsar Nicholas I.

evidence.title: Nikolay Speshnev
evidence.text: Nikolay Alexandrovich Speshnev (Russian: Николай Александрович Спе́шнев; 1821, Kursk - 1882, St. Petersburg) was a 19th-century Russian aristocrat and political activist, best known for his involvement with the pro-socialist literary discussion group the Petrashevsky Circle.

evidence.title: Nikolay Speshnev
evidence.text: He formed a secret revolutionary society from among the members of the circle, which included the young Fyodor Dostoevsky.

evidence.title: Nikolay Speshnev
evidence.text: After the government of Tsar Nicholas I arrested the members of the Petrashevsky Circle in 1849, Speshnev was interrogated, threatened with torture, and eventually sentenced, along with Dostoevsky, Petrashevsky and others, to execution by firing squad.

evidence.title: Nikolay Speshnev
evidence.text: The sentence was commuted to hard labour in Siberia, but the prisoners were only informed of this after enduring a mock execution.

evidence.title: Norma Guillard
evidence.text: Norma Guillard Limonta is a Cuban social psychologist and adjunct lecturer at the University of Havana.

evidence.title: Norma Guillard
evidence.text: She is a co-founder of Grupo Oremi, a now defunct lesbian discussion group in Cuba.

evidence.title: Norma Guillard
evidence.text: Her academic works borders on gender, sexuality, race and identity.

evidence.title: Norma Guillard
evidence.text: Guillard is a foundation member of the Cuban branch of La Articulacion Regional de Afrodescendientes de Latinoamerica y el Caribe, a joint regional discussion group composed of individuals of African descent in Latin America and the Caribbean.
